jurisdiction.name: Denmark
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Denmark applies the EU AI Act through Act 467/2025, in force since August 2025, which designates the Agency for Digital Government, the Data Protection Agency and the Court Administration as national authorities; a replacement AI Act bill and a copyright bill against deepfakes of a person's likeness were introduced in October 2026. Policy follows the 2024 all-party digitalisation strategy and a December 2024 strategic approach to AI, replacing the 2019 national strategy. Denmark also gives public bodies explicit legal bases for using AI through sector laws and executive orders, and the Agency for Digital Government, the Data Protection Agency and the Financial Supervisory Authority have issued AI guidance.
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The new AI Act bill and the deepfake copyright bill are listed as leads, and two records could only be located because the official pages give no date.

instruments.official_title: Strategisk indsats for kunstig intelligens
instruments.english_title: Strategic Approach to Artificial Intelligence
instruments.current_status: Presented 2 December 2024 by the Minister of Digital Affairs; the official English edition is recorded here (Danish original 'Strategisk indsats for kunstig intelligens', December 2024, available as a Folketing committee appendix). Cover date is December 2024 only.
instruments.summary: The government's December 2024 strategic AI initiative, 'a more robust foundation for the responsible development and use of AI in Denmark', implementing the AI pillar of the 2024 digitalisation strategy. It launches four initiatives: a Digital Taskforce for AI to roll out AI in the public sector at scale, a research-based centre advising on responsible AI, secure and transparent Danish language models, and open Danish data for AI, funded with DKK 62.5 million for 2024-2027 plus further allocations.

instruments.english_title: National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Industry, Business and Financial Affairs (Finansministeriet og Erhvervsministeriet)
instruments.current_status: Published March 2019 by the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Industry, Business and Financial Affairs (hosted on em.dk and regeringen.dk; an English edition was published by the government at the time). Treated as superseded by the February 2024 all-party digitalisation strategy agreement and the December 2024 Strategic Approach to Artificial Intelligence, which now set Denmark's AI direction (no official repeal notice).
instruments.summary: Denmark's first national AI strategy (March 2019) set a vision for Denmark to be a frontrunner in responsible AI, with 24 initiatives and DKK 60 million set aside for 2019-2027. Its focus areas were a responsible foundation for AI including six ethical principles, more and better data, strong competences and new knowledge, and increased investment, with signature projects in the public sector.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First national AI strategy; source of Denmark's AI ethics principles; replaced in practice by the 2024 digitalisation strategy and Strategic Approach to AI.

instruments.summary: All-party political agreement of 8 February 2024 setting Denmark's digitalisation strategy: 29 initiatives and DKK 740 million for 2024-2027 across the public and private sectors. Its AI pillar ('a responsible and strong foundation for using AI') launches a strategic AI initiative, a regulatory sandbox for AI run with the Data Protection Agency, and Danish language data for training language models.

instruments.official_title: Lov om supplerende bestemmelser til forordningen om kunstig intelligens
instruments.english_title: Act on Supplementary Provisions to the Regulation on Artificial Intelligence (Act No. 467 of 14 May 2025)
instruments.current_status: In force since 2 August 2025 (status 'Gældende' on Retsinformation, 12 October 2026). Bill L 154 (2024-25) introduced 26 February 2025. A replacement 'AI-loven' (bill L 3, introduced 7 October 2026) would repeal this Act and let the minister designate market surveillance authorities by order; it is pending (see leads).
instruments.summary: Danish law implementing the EU AI Act's governance provisions. It designates the Agency for Digital Government, the Data Protection Agency and the Danish Court Administration as national competent authorities (the Agency for Digital Government as notifying authority, single point of contact and market surveillance authority for most Art. 5 prohibitions; the Data Protection Agency for Art. 5(1)(d) and (g)), gives them powers to demand information, inspect premises without a court order, publish decisions and issue orders or temporary bans, and makes breaches of the prohibitions punishable by fines.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Denmark's AI Act implementing law; designates national AI supervisory authorities.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): Retsinformation PDF (api/pdf/249582) read in full; LOV nr 467 af 14/05/2025 (Gældende); § 12 entry into force 2 August 2025

instruments.current_status: Consolidated text LBK 289/2024 is the current version ('Gældende') on Retsinformation as of 12 October 2026; original Act no. 502 of 23 May 2018.
instruments.summary: Denmark's Data Protection Act supplementing the GDPR, consolidated as LBK no. 289 of 8 March 2024. It sets national rules on legal bases (including research and statistics under § 10), special categories of data, data subjects' rights, the Data Protection Agency's powers and penalties, which govern the processing of personal data when AI systems are trained and used.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law that governs AI training and use; the Data Protection Agency's AI guidance builds on it.

instruments.summary: Agency for Digital Government note helping public authorities adopt generative AI responsibly. It explains what generative AI is and recommends that each authority decide its approach to tools, distinguish general staff use from specialised projects, set internal guidelines (e.g. on personal and confidential data, checking outputs, transparency) and build staff competences, with reference to the GDPR and the AI Act.

instruments.english_title: Guidance: Measures to secure the use of artificial intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Agency for Digital Government, Danish Business Authority and Centre for Cyber Security
instruments.current_status: Published January 2020; prepared with Globeteam and Boston Consulting Group. No newer version found.
instruments.summary: Guidance for Danish companies and public authorities on information-security measures when developing and using AI, issued under the 2019 national AI strategy and the national cyber and information security strategy. It explains four AI-specific attack types (such as data poisoning, adversarial attacks, backdoors and data extraction) and sets out 16 concrete measures for management, AI developers and system owners, to be used alongside ISO 27001 and general security guidance.

instruments.official_title: Anbefalinger om brug af generativ AI i undervisningen i folkeskolen
instruments.english_title: Recommendations on the use of generative AI in teaching in the Folkeskole (primary and lower-secondary school)
instruments.issuing_authority: Styrelsen for Undervisning og Kvalitet, Børne- og Undervisningsministeriet (Danish Agency for Education and Quality, Ministry of Children and Education)
instruments.publisher_name: Danish Agency for Education and Quality
instruments.current_status: Published June 2025 (colophon date). Non-binding recommendations; the document notes there are no national guidelines on how generative AI may be used in Folkeskole teaching and that students may not use generative AI in exams. Adapted from the agency's November 2024 recommendations for upper-secondary and vocational education.
instruments.summary: National recommendations for school leaders, teachers, pedagogues, school boards and school administrations on using generative AI in Folkeskole teaching. Its seven recommendations advise schools to set a shared direction and framework for generative AI use, use only GDPR-compliant solutions, support staff dialogue and competence development, use generative AI only when it makes subject, didactic and pedagogical sense, talk with students about how, when and why they may use it in each subject, and inform parents about the school's approach.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National ministry guidance setting the frame for generative AI use in primary and lower-secondary school teaching.

instruments.summary: Ten recommendations for leaders and teachers at Danish upper-secondary schools (gymnasiale uddannelser) on generative AI in teaching. School leadership should set a shared direction and concrete common rules for teachers' and students' use, use solutions it judges to comply with the GDPR and prioritise teachers' competence; teachers should use generative AI only where it makes subject, didactic and pedagogical sense and build students' critically reflective use. Exams are dealt with in a separate publication by the expert group on ChatGPT and other digital aids.

organizations.ai_governance_role: Datatilsynet; data protection authority; market surveillance authority for AI Act Art. 5(1)(d) and (g) prohibitions under Law 467/2025; issues AI guidance for public authorities and co-runs the regulatory AI sandbox.

organizations.name: Danish Financial Supervisory Authority
organizations.ai_governance_role: Finanstilsynet; financial supervisor; published good-practice papers on AI use (2019, 2024) and a 2024 survey of AI use in the financial sector.

organizations.name: Ministry of Finance
organizations.ai_governance_role: Finansministeriet; co-issued the 2019 National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence.

organizations.name: Danish Parliament
organizations.ai_governance_role: Folketinget; adopts AI-related legislation, including Law 467/2025 supplementing the EU AI Act and the AI provisions in the SU Act and employment legislation.

organizations.name: Ministry of Employment
organizations.ai_governance_role: Beskæftigelsesministeriet (Beskæftigelses- og Ligestillingsministeriet); issued executive orders on AI use by the Danish Working Environment Authority, the Danish Agency for Labour Market and Recruitment and municipal job centres.

organizations.name: Ministry of Higher Education and Science
organizations.ai_governance_role: Uddannelses- og Forskningsministeriet (from 2026 Forsknings-, Uddannelses- og Digitaliseringsministeriet); sponsored the 2025 SU Act amendment allowing AI-supported case processing and the executive orders under it.

organizations.name: Ministry of Justice
organizations.ai_governance_role: Justitsministeriet; responsible for the Danish Data Protection Act (databeskyttelsesloven).

organizations.name: Danish Agency for Education and Quality
organizations.ai_governance_role: Styrelsen for Undervisning og Kvalitet, an agency of the Ministry of Children and Education; publishes the national recommendations on generative AI in teaching for the Folkeskole, upper-secondary and vocational education.

organizations.name: Danish Digitalisation Council
organizations.ai_governance_role: Digitaliseringsrådet, an advisory council set up by the Government in September 2022 (a chair and 10 members from the public and private sectors); issued an AI vision (June 2023) and operational AI recommendations (February 2024).

organizations.name: Ministry of Senior Citizens
organizations.ai_governance_role: Ældreministeriet; responsible for the Eldercare Act, including the draft amendment empowering the minister to set rules on AI in eldercare.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: The official legal database, the digital ministry and the Agency for Digital Government, other ministries and regulators were searched at national level. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for procurement, transparency, standards, drafts and consultations, or international agreements. Not yet verified from the official text: the Danish Parliament's AI material, the education ministry's school AI recommendations (not found at their known addresses) and the launch date of the AI sandbox.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. ft.dk behind a bot challenge (Folketing papers not read); uvm.dk school recommendations 404 (lead). Sandbox page has no launch date and the Finanstilsynet survey date is PDF metadata only (both located only). 2019 strategy marked superseded by the 2024 documents (no formal repeal). Convention 108: BKI nr 59 af 16/05/1991 (title, number and date from Retsinformation's official search; full text not rendered), recorded on the COE file. Units covered: Law: Retsinformation searched (AI law, AI provisions, AI Act implementation, data protection, deepfake/copyright, Convention 108): Act 467/2025, Data Protection Act, SU Act amendment 674/2025 and 4 executive orders on public-sector AI use recorded; AI-loven bill L 3 and copyright/deepfake bill L 49 (both introduced Oct 2026) held as leads. ft.dk blocked by a bot challenge.; Government: Digital ministry and Agency for Digital Government: 2019 national strategy (superseded), 2024 digitalisation strategy agreement, Dec 2024 Strategic Approach to AI, GenAI guides for authorities and businesses, regulatory AI sandbox recorded.; Ministries: Employment (3 AI executive orders), Higher Education/Research (SU AI law and order), Justice (Data Protection Act) recorded; Children and Education GenAI recommendations located but URLs 404 (lead); health, defence, tax: searched, nothing AI-specific found.; Regulators: Datatilsynet (2023 public-sector AI guidance) and Finanstilsynet (2024 good practice, 2024 survey) recorded; cyber: 2020 AI security guidance co-issued with the Centre for Cyber Security recorded (no newer CFCS/SAMSIK AI document found); competition (KFST), telecom/media, health (Sundhedsstyrelsen, Lægemiddelstyrelsen): searched, nothing AI-specific found.; Other: Procurement (no national AI procurement guidance found), standards (Dansk Standard sells ISO/IEC 42001 but no Danish DS adoption confirmed on an official page), transparency (no algorithm register found): searched, nothing found. Drafts: AI-loven bill L 3 and copyright/deepfake bill L 49 held as leads (pending bills).. Not reached: none. Could not verify: Convention 108 BKI 59/1991: only title/number/date from the Retsinformation search API; full text not rendered; Regulatory AI sandbox launch date (page states none); Finanstilsynet 2024 AI survey publication date (from PDF metadata only); ft.dk documents (bot challenge): Danish edition of the Strategic Approach, committee papers; uvm.dk GenAI recommendations for schools (404 at known URLs). procurement, transparency, standards, drafts, international: no material found.
Wording note 2026-10-19 (coverage_audit.no_material_found_note): The Danish Parliament's site was unavailable and the education ministry's school AI recommendations could not be found at their known addresses, so these, together with the launch date of the AI sandbox, remain to be checked.

leads.title: Forslag til Lov om supplerende bestemmelser til forordningen om kunstig intelligens (AI-loven) (L 3, 2026-27)
leads.english_title: Bill on supplementary provisions to the AI Regulation (the AI Act bill), L 3 of 2026-27
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Research, Education and Digital Affairs (Forsknings-, Uddannelses- og Digitaliseringsministeriet)
leads.note: Introduced in the Folketing on 7 October 2026 (Retsinformation 2026/1 LSF 3, https://www.retsinformation.dk/eli/ft/202612L00003; text read via api/pdf/257974). It would repeal Act 467/2025, let the minister designate national competent and market surveillance authorities by order, keep the Agency for Digital Government as single point of contact and coordinator, add blocking of online interfaces and fines; in force the day after promulgation. Earlier version L 111 (2025-26, introduced February 2026) apparently lapsed. Promote when adopted.

leads.title: Forslag til Lov om ændring af lov om ophavsret (Beskyttelse af personlige kendetegn m.v. og ændret proces for prøvelse ved Ophavsretslicensnævnet) (L 49, 2026-27)
leads.english_title: Bill amending the Copyright Act (protection of personal characteristics against realistic digital imitations / deepfakes, etc.), L 49 of 2026-27
leads.note: Introduced 8 October 2026 by the Minister of Culture (Retsinformation 2026/1 LSF 49, read via api/pdf/258147). New § 73 a would prohibit making available realistic digitally generated imitations of a natural person's personal, physical characteristics without consent (deepfakes), with extended protection for performing artists; proposed entry into force 1 January 2027. Promote when adopted.

leads.title: Regulatorisk sandkasse for AI
leads.issuing_authority: Agency for Digital Government and Danish Data Protection Agency
leads.note: Moved from records by the date audit (2026-10-13): no publication date is stated by the issuer. Issuer pages (digst.dk sandbox page and its 'Afsluttede forløb' subpage; datatilsynet.dk regulatorisk-sandkasse page) state no launch/establishment date; they say only that the sandbox was established 'som led i regeringens digitaliseringsstrategi'. 2024 is inferred from the 8 Feb 2024 strategy agreement, which is not a launch date. Secondary sources (securityworldmarket.dk, Dansk Erhverv event March 2024) say launched March 2024, but no issuer launch notice found. Needs human decision: an operating sandbox rather than a document Official URL: https://digst.dk/tilsyn/ai-forordningen/regulatorisk-sandkasse-for-ai/. Previously recorded as administrative_guideline, publication_date 2024. Update 2026-11-07: Datatilsynet's Annual Report 2025 (foreword 'Valby, marts 2026'; https://cdn1.gopublic.dk/datatilsynet/Media/639105380237831502/Datatilsynets årsberetning 2025.pdf) states that Datatilsynet, together with Digitaliseringsstyrelsen, launched the regulatory AI sandbox in March 2024; the first two sandbox reports (Tryg; the Talt project) were published in October 2025. This issuer statement supplies the launch date (2024-03) if the sandbox is re-recorded.
